title: Mixing modern and traditional at festivals
summary: He prefers festivals that mix styles, since modern or traditional bills sound repetitive, and describes Berne and Breda.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, there are some--- I think - of course, when they say - a traditional jazz festival--
Well, I think--- I prefer a festival that has both kinds of music---
Because I think-- you know, if you go sit and listen to a modern festival - George Wein has put on a modern festival; I heard one once and it's over and over you're hearing the same thing---
Well, a lot of Newport's modern now.

Yeah but you're hearing the same thing over and over and over again because I think the modern bands don't play that different from one another and I suppose the traditional guys don't play too much different from one another. The only thing that would make a difference would be the selection of songs you're going to play--

But, I think the best festivals in Europe and some here have done that too -- where they mix it up a little and I think that's good for the attendance too because everybody doesn't like to sit and listen to traditional for seven days of traditional music anymore than-- they like to have something to break it up. Maybe a band like Basie or those kind of things happening - you know - and they've been doing that in Europe and they do it at the Berne festival where I play now; they always
have a modern or a big band sound, you know -- now, this year - of course, they'll have Peanuts Hucko with the big band at Berne.
